links.outcome: Diagnostic AUC and errors for radiologists with vs without AI, and AI alone
links.effect: Combined AUC 0.928-0.934 vs manual 0.888-0.914 and AI alone 0.807-0.810; errors 7 combined vs 29 manual vs 43 AI alone; overall manual vs combined P=0.0427.
links.quote: The combined radiologist + AI approach resulted in only 7 diagnostic errors (2 false-negative and 5 false-positive cases), representing a 75.9% reduction in errors compared to AI alone and a 75.9% reduction compared to radiologists alone.

links.outcome: Radiologist performance with AI in intended workflow versus standalone AI metrics
links.effect: Standalone AI AUC 0.807-0.810 was below radiologists (0.888-0.914); combined reading reached 0.928-0.934, significantly above AI alone in all centers.
links.quote: DeLong test comparisons revealed statistically significant improvements in AUC for the combined approach compared to either AI-only or radiologist-only interpretation across all centers (P < 0.05 for all comparisons).

links.outcome: AI compared with radiologists on the same data for PE detection
links.effect: AI alone AUC 0.807-0.810 was lower than manual reading AUC 0.888-0.914; AI had 43 errors versus 29 for radiologists.
links.quote: The findings of our comprehensive analysis reveal a persistent performance gap between standalone AI systems and experienced radiologists in PE detection.

links.outcome: Adjunct (radiologist plus AI) versus AI standalone diagnostic accuracy
links.effect: AI alone had 43 errors (36 false positives); radiologist plus AI had 7 errors and higher AUC 0.928-0.934 than AI alone 0.807-0.810.
links.quote: The superior performance of the combined approach suggests that AI systems function most effectively as assistive tools rather than replacement technologies, augmenting human expertise rather than superseding it.

links.outcome: AI performance reported separately by site and scanner
links.effect: AI AUC was consistent across three centers (0.807-0.810) despite one center using a 128-slice scanner; correlation PTBS-PAOI r 0.824-0.909. Regional and scanner uniformity limit generalizability.
links.quote: Although our multicenter design involved three hospitals employing predominantly 256-slice CT scanners and one center using 128-slice CT, all within Xinjiang, China, this regional and scanner uniformity may limit the generalizability of the results.

links.outcome: Interrater reliability of consensus reference standard
links.effect: Pairwise Cohen's kappa 0.867-0.894 and Fleiss' kappa 0.884 among three senior radiologists.
links.quote: The overall interrater agreement among the three radiologists was also excellent, with a Fleiss’ Kappa value of 0.884 (P < 0.001).

links.effect: Combined manual+AI AUC 0.928–0.934 vs AI alone 0.807–0.810 and manual alone 0.888–0.914.
links.quote: Our results demonstrate that the AUC for the combined radiologist and AI reading approach (92.81%–93.38%) was substantially superior to both radiologists working independently (88.79%–91.43%) and AI systems operating in isolation (80.72%–81%).

links.outcome: Human-AI team performance and reading time
links.effect: AI+manual time was 2.61 ± 0.69 min vs manual 5.26 ± 0.94 min, with superior diagnostic accuracy.
links.quote: The combined AI-assisted approach yielded intermediate processing times of 2.61 ± 0.69 min, achieving a 50% reduction in interpretation time compared to manual reading alone while maintaining superior diagnostic accuracy.
